A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BoxDreamer and provide readable methods, equations, experiments, seven tables and five figures. All 11 pages of each were inspected. Neither includes an appendix; the supplementary material referenced by both is not supplied and cannot be assessed.

before.justification: v1 reports original pose-estimation experiments on LINEMOD, Occluded LINEMOD, YCB-Video and OnePose-LowTexture, together with robustness analyses, training ablations and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical experiments and analyses, with localized revisions to accuracy values and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 changes the specified heatmap construction from a shared scale based on average squared corner distances to a scale based on each corner's distance from the object center. The reconstruction, transformer, losses and PnP pipeline remain. The PDFs do not establish whether this reflects an implementation change or a reporting correction.

E1.justification: Training remains based on Objaverse and OnePose. The reported evaluation coverage remains LINEMOD, Occluded LINEMOD, YCB-Video and OnePose-LowTexture, including the same three YCB reference-database scenarios. Both versions also refer to OnePose results in unavailable supplementary material.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within the corresponding tables: OnePose++, Gen6D variants, Cas6D and GS-Pose variants in Table 1; PoseCNN and PVNet alongside the generalizable baselines in Table 2; and the same comparators in Tables 3–5.

E3.justification: Section 3.4 removes inserting images of other objects from the stated occlusion augmentations, retaining truncation and masking. Section 4.5 changes the runtime workload from 10 to 5 reference images. These are reported setting revisions; the PDFs do not establish that the benchmark experiments were rerun. Splits, metrics and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The reference-count sensitivity analysis in Figure 4, noisy-box robustness analysis in Figure 5 and Table 6, real-data training ablation in Table 7, and qualitative occlusion comparisons in Figure 3 retain the same evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for its experiments. The reporting practice remains point estimates and averages across objects.

E6.justification: In Table 2's five-reference ADD(s)-0.1d results, BoxDreamer's duck score changes from 42.8 to 16.1 and its average from 29.8 to 26.5; Gen6D with ground-truth detections changes from 5.2 to 5.4 on duck. Other table values are retained. Section 4.5 replaces 23 ms inference and 11 s reconstruction with 17 ms and 5.3 s, respectively, while changing from 10 to 5 references; this does not establish a same-setting speedup.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 revises a mathematical definition: v1 sets sigma to one-tenth of the average squared corner-to-center pixel distance, whereas v2 sets 2 sigma squared to the square of one-tenth of each corner's pixel distance to the 2D center. The displayed kernel, projection, filtering and loss equations otherwise retain their substance. Neither version provides formal proofs.

C1.justification: The contribution list replaces 'The first to propose' bounding-box corners for practical pose estimation with 'We propose' them for generalizable pose estimation. Section 2.3 likewise removes the explicit priority claim. The abstract and conclusion retain the main generalization, occlusion-robustness and real-time claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of sparse-view performance, occlusion handling, noisy-box tolerance and real-data training remain unchanged, as do limitations concerning symmetry, memory and separate detection. The added statement that reconstruction occurs once offline makes the existing pre-inference setup distinction explicit without introducing a new applicability boundary.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 newly states that heatmap channels correspond to corners through a predefined ordering. Heatmap-scale, augmentation and runtime details are revised, and the new acknowledgment identifies the RoboSense AC1 sensor used for some data collection and validation. The same project URL is retained; its relocation does not establish changed code availability.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 softens the claim of being first to use bounding-box corners for generalizable pose estimation. The cited research coverage otherwise remains unchanged: v1's duplicate entries for the Cas6D paper are consolidated in v2, rather than a distinct prior work being removed.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording and terminology edits, clarifies the correspondence explanation, adjusts subsection titles, updates affiliations and adds acknowledgments. The main section hierarchy and narrative remain intact; this is not an extensive rewrite or reorganization.

P2.justification: Table 5 moves from page 8 to page 7. Table captions now explain ranking colors and boldface, and best values receive additional bold emphasis. Figure 4 and Table 7 receive clearer captions, with modest figure sizing and page-layout adjustments. No figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves technical clarity through the explicit channel-to-corner convention and revised heatmap-scale specification, softens broad priority claims, and explains table highlighting. The empirical support remains largely unchanged. Revised scores are not independently validated by the PDFs, and the smaller timing workload does not demonstrate acceleration, so the evidence supports a limited improvement in documentation and presentation.
